newsitem.title: DJIBOUTI: Seven African states to relaunch development plan.
newsitem.headline: Seven African states to relaunch development plan.

text.p: Ministers from seven eastern African states met in Djibouti on Sunday to prepare for the launching of a new development initiative covering the Horn of Africa and nearby states.

Heads of State are due to inaugurate the revamped Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) -- covering Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan and Uganda -- on Monday, to spur peace and development in the region.

The grouping was originally launched in 1986, after disastrous drought in the Horn of Africa, as the Intergovernmental Authority on Drought and Development (IGADD) to counter famine in the region. It will now have a wider aim covering political as well as development issues.
Opening the ministers' meeting, Djibouti Foreign Minister Mohamed Moussa Chehem said problems of peace and security in the region were hampering efforts to spur development.
IGAD secretary-general Tekeste Gebray said a new division was being launched to prevent, manage and resolve conflicts between member states.
Its immediate task would be to reactivate initiatives for peace and security in the Sudan and Somalia -- countries with a long history of internal conflict.
But little could be achieved until the organisation's finances improved, the secretary-general said.

Member states owe more than $2.34 million -- equal to IGAD's total budget for a year and a half. Sudan, Uganda, Kenya and Somalia were named those in arrears. IGAD's bank overdraft has reached $500,000.
Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka, chairing the ministerial meeting, said the reorganisation of the regional group was supported by other states and by the Organisation of African Unity.
